The MIG journal club is run by
[Melbourne Integrative Genomics](https://research.unimelb.edu.au/integrative-genomics)
at the University of Melbourne. We read one paper — occasionally a small set —
and discuss it properly for an hour.

Papers are chosen mainly by whoever is presenting. We will also discuss towards the end of each session what papers the audience what to see. Example topics include (not limited to): 

- single-cell and spatial omics; 
- multi-omics integration; 
- methods in microbiology, ecology and marine sciences; 
- statistical and causal inference;
- machine learning for biology;
- 'meta-science' (how science is done). 


## When we meet

Monthly, on a Thursday at 3:30 pm, in Room 124, Building 184. See the
[next meeting](index.qmd) for the current date.

## How to join

Anyone interested is welcome — MIG members, people elsewhere at the University and affiliated institutes,
visitors. There is no membership and no commitment to attend regularly.

To be added to the meeting invitations, contact [**Jiadong Mao**](mailto:jiadong.mao@unimelb.edu.au).


## Do I need to read the paper before the session?

You are welcome to come without having read the paper. Most people have skimmed
it; a few have read it closely; the discussion is built to work either way.

## How meetings are recorded and published

**Meetings are audio-recorded for edited transcripts to be published.** Please read
this section before your first meeting.

- The recording is used only to compile the report, and the recording itself is not published.
- Reports name the **presenter**, and may name people who proposed follow-up
  reading. Other contributions are attributed anonymously — "it was noted",
  "one attendee argued" — because room microphones do not always separate speakers
  reliably.
- Every report is reviewed by someone other than its author before it is
  published. That review checks the science, and also checks that criticism is
  aimed at the work rather than at the people who did it.
- **You can ask not to be named**, before or after a meeting, with no reason
  needed. Tell an organiser and the attribution is removed. (You can also pick a pseudonym, say Socrates.)
  
Discussion here is often critical, sometimes sharply. That is the point of a
journal club. It is published in the spirit of open scientific disagreement, and
we try hard to keep it directed at the work. If you are an author of something we
have discussed and feel we have got you wrong,
[open an issue](https://github.com/melbintgen/mig-journal-club/issues/new) — we
will correct it, and you are very welcome to reply.

## Presenting

Presenting is informal: pick a paper you want to think about, bring it, and lead
the discussion. You do not need slides, although slides are recommended. See
[contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) if you would like to report on your own session,
or [propose a paper](https://github.com/melbintgen/mig-journal-club/issues/new?template=propose-paper.yml)
for someone else to present.
